newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Labour, Alliance meeting adjourns for lunch.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Labour, Alliance meeting adjourns for lunch.

text.p: The centre-left Labour Party and left-wing Alliance broke from their meeting at 2.30 p.m. for a lunch adjournment.
The meeting, called to discuss Alliance support for a possible coalition between Labour and the nationalist New Zealand First Party, began at 11.30 a.m.
Labour leader Helen Clark said the two parties would meet for as long as it took to reach a resolution.
"We are talking about the matters that are necessary for the Alliance to know in order to give an assurance of confidence on (money) supply," she told reporters.
Alliance leader Jim Anderton said the meeting so far had been positive and constructive. He earlier told reporters he may need more than one meeting with Labour.
"We will work until we finish," he said.
Labour and NZ First would jointly hold 54 seats in the 120-member parliament, and would need the support of the 13 Alliance MPs on money supply and confidence votes.
Anderton has consistently said he will not give a "blank cheque" promise of support without being briefed and consulted on the policy programme of such a government.
NZ First is also negotiating with the caretaker National Party government, and is expected to announce its decision on Tuesday. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
